1	[Resource from github at repo://missingbulb/edfringenow/sha/35005df09923192ba459e03049a83516cbab2708/contents/product-wiki/festival-circuits/README.md] # The festival circuits
2	
3	The world's comedy festivals as a market: what exists, what shape each one is,
4	and what it would take to point EdFringeNow's planning product at any of them.
5	This page exists because the owner's direction (2026-09-01) is to grow
6	EdFringeNow into a festival-planning product, and the first expansion axis is
7	the art form the product already serves best — comedy is the Fringe's largest
8	genre. Compiled once, refined in place.
9	
10	Division of labour with the neighbouring pages:
11	[festmaxxing-environments/](../festmaxxing-environments/README.md)
12	owns the *city* question (which cities carry the Edinburgh-in-August overwhelm
13	pattern, whatever the art form); this page owns the *comedy festival* question —
14	the worldwide circuit, each festival's structure, organizer, ticketing and data
15	reachability — plus a deliberately light survey of the **film** festivals that
16	share the planner-complex shape (its own section below). Planner-type
17	competitors found along the way live on
18	[competitor-landscape/](../competitor-landscape/README.md).
19	
20	## Key insights
21	
22	- Only ~8 of 85 census festivals are fringe-shaped. Most of the circuit is one-night showcases with nothing to schedule.
23	- MICF is the southern Edinburgh — 803 shows, 9,164 performances, open registration — with unauthenticated JSON APIs.
24	- Leicester's operator went bust in Aug 2026 owing performers ticket money. Feb 2027 is two rival reboots.
25	- Nearly everything is annual in the same city, but brands churn: JFL survived receivership, Netflix Is A Joke is biennial.
26	- Recurrence decides planning — in film too: Fringe shows play ~14 times, Berlinale screens films up to 5×, US one-offs are terminal.
27	- Leicester and Brighton share one platform (Eventotron) and identical open APIs — one adapter reads both.

127	Competition** ("across the Bay Area") and **Seattle International Comedy
128	Competition** ("all month across Western Washington", November), both
129	month-long *touring competitions* rather than city takeovers, and **Just For
130	Laughs Singapore** (tbd) — plus the first 2027 confirmations (JFL Bermuda,
131	17–20 Feb 2027; SXSW, 17–20 Mar 2027). The tracker's own dates are treated
132	here as launch-time claims, not delivered totals — and the dossiers below
133	correct five of its entries against primary sources: Roundhouse actually ran
134	1–18 Aug, Greenwich has rebranded to "Comedy Garden", the "Dublin Comedy
135	Festival" is a suburban pub circuit, JFL Paris appears dead, and
136	Machynlleth (the UK's best small-town takeover) is missing entirely.
137	
138	What the census says before any per-festival research:
139	
140	- **The circuit is mostly weekend showcases.** 45 of 85 dated festivals run ≤4
141	  days, and 56 of 85 are in the US — overwhelmingly club-scale, curated or
142	  submission-based weekends where a visitor picks a headliner, not a schedule.
143	- **The fringe-length tier is small and un-American.** Only 13 festivals run
144	  ≥14 days, and the US contributes just two (SF Sketchfest and the new Fallout
145	  Fringe in Las Vegas); the other eleven are UK, Irish, Australian and NZ
146	  events — Edinburgh, Adelaide, Brighton, Melbourne, Sydney Comedy Festival,
147	  JFL Sydney, NZICF, Leicester, Aberdeen, the London Clown Festival, and the
148	  Dublin entry examined below.
149	- **Run length is a strong first classifier.** A festival long enough to need
150	  repeat performances of the same show is where a scheduling product has work
151	  to do; a weekend of one-night showcases is not. The dossiers below test that
152	  presumption festival by festival.
153	
154	## The two shapes, and what decides planner-worthiness
155	
156	The owner's framing question — which festivals behave like the Fringe and
157	which like music festivals — turns out to rest on two measurable axes, and
158	the dossiers below supply the numbers:
159	
160	1. **Parallel volume**: how many shows run at once. Edinburgh peaks in the
161	   thousands per day; MICF at ~350; Leicester's own API shows 242 on its
162	   peak Saturday; Netflix Is A Joke ~100; Sydney ~29; most of the census
163	   runs single digits. Below a few dozen parallel shows, "which can I make"
164	   stops being a problem a product needs to solve.
165	2. **Recurrence**: how many times one show plays. Edinburgh averages ~14
166	   performances per show and MICF ~11 — miss tonight, catch tomorrow, so
167	   planning is *packing*. Sydney averages 2.4 and Leicester 2.28; the US
168	   majors run one-night events almost exclusively — every clash is
169	   terminal, so planning is *triage*, and with few parallel shows it
170	   reduces to picking headliners.
171	
172	Two more axes modulate the answer: **venue geography** (a walkable core —
173	Edinburgh, MICF's CBD, Machynlleth — makes multi-show days physically
174	possible; a car city like LA or Dubai caps a day at one neighbourhood;
175	a single site has nothing to route) and **access model** (open access —
176	anyone who pays registers — is what produces uncapped supply; curation caps
177	it by construction).
178	
179	The resulting map of the census:
180	
181	- **Fringe-shaped** (open access, repeated runs, many venues, real clash
182	  grid): Edinburgh, Adelaide, **MICF**, **Brighton** (46% comedy), and
183	  **Leicester** in its short-visit variant — plus **NZICF** small and
184	  **Machynlleth** miniature. This is the entire planner-market tier, and
185	  outside Edinburgh none of it has a third-party planner
186	  ([competitor-landscape/](../competitor-landscape/README.md)).
187	- **Showcase-shaped** (curated one-nighters, pick-your-headliner): the JFL
188	  empire, NYCF, Sydney, Perth, Galway, Dubai, Aberdeen, Winnipeg, Halifax,
189	  Nashville, 312, and — at fringe *breadth* but one-off depth — SF
190	  Sketchfest and Netflix Is A Joke, where the planning problem is real but
191	  is scarcity-triage (nothing repeats) rather than schedule-packing.
192	- **Distinct sub-shapes the two poles don't cover**: the **badge-graze**
193	  festivals (Moontower's club binge, Del Close Marathon, SXSW) where entry
194	  is walk-in and the constraint is room capacity, not tickets; the
195	  **roving franchise** (Great Outdoors; 57 Festivals' Comedy Gardens) — one
196	  stage, touring cities; the **anti-planner compound** (Skankfest, schedule
197	  released day-of); the **touring competitions** (Boston's bracket, SF and
198	  Seattle's month-long circuits); the **TV-taping festivals** (Winnipeg,
199	  Halifax — the broadcast is the product); the **venue season** (Aberdeen,
200	  Roundhouse); the **club hub** (Tokyo, Grindstone); and the **pub circuit**
201	  wearing a festival name (the "Dublin Comedy Festival").
202	
203	The product read: **run length in the census predicts the shape but does
204	not decide it** — Sydney (35 days) and Aberdeen (16) are showcases, while
205	Machynlleth (3 days) has a denser grid than either. The deciding pair is
206	parallel volume × recurrence, and only the fringe-shaped tier scores high
207	on both.
208	
209	## The fringe-shaped tier: dossiers
210	
211	The festivals where "which of tonight's shows can I make" is a real problem —
212	long runs, repeated performances, many parallel rooms. This is the tier a
213	planning product can serve.
214	
215	### Melbourne International Comedy Festival — the southern Edinburgh
216	
217	The standout of the whole census, and the closest thing to a second Edinburgh
218	Fringe anywhere in comedy.
219	
220	- **Scale, delivered 2026** (the festival's own
221	  [40th-year wrap](https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/news/celebrating-a-record-40th-year/)):
222	  **803 shows and events, 9,164 performances, 26 days** (25 Mar–19 Apr),
223	  796,975 attendees (+13% YoY), A$26.6m box office, average paid ticket
224	  A$38.20. That is ~350 performances a day — genuinely fringe-like clash
225	  density. Launch press said "over 750 shows", so ~50 more landed after
226	  launch: the launch-undercount trap
227	  [edinburgh-market-and-audience/](../edinburgh-market-and-audience/README.md) documents holds
228	  here too.
229	- **Show model**: Edinburgh-style seasons — one show is the same hour repeated
230	  across the run (sampled runs of 7–24 performances; cheaper previews,
231	  cheap-Tuesday flags). Participation is **open registration**
232	  ([registrations open each October](https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/participate/),
233	  with independent venues found via a venue finder) — the Fringe's
234	  open-access mechanism, at ~one-fifth Edinburgh's scale.
235	- **Organizer & recurrence**: its own festival organization, annual every
236	  autumn since 1987, always Melbourne, centred on Melbourne Town Hall;
237	  [self-described](https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/about-us/) as "one of
238	  the three largest comedy festivals in the world, alongside Edinburgh
239	  Festival Fringe and Montreal's Just for Laughs" and "Australia's largest
240	  ticketed cultural event". Stable through a 2026 leadership handover
241	  (Susan Provan retired after 32 years;
242	  [Dylan Cole appointed CEO/Festival Director](https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/news/melbourne-international-comedy-festival-appoints-dylan-cole-as-new-ceofestival-director/)).

249	  share-a-favourites-list); a minority of external-venue shows link out to
250	  Ticketmaster/Ticketek/Arts Centre Melbourne.

252	  verified by fetch:
253	  `POST /umbraco/api/searchapi/searchShows` (826 show records for 2026, paged,
254	  with runs, performance counts, venue rooms),
255	  `GET /umbraco/api/venuesapi/getvenues` (all 143 venues with address,
256	  capacity, accessibility flags), and each show page embeds a `sessionData`

260	  [sitemap](https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/sitemap.xml) lists every show
261	  URL.

263	  overlap the window, with the AFL season running throughout (per

265	  — city-draw amplifiers, though nothing on the scale of Edinburgh's August
266	  cluster.
267	- **Planner field**: the site's account favourites are the only planning tool;
268	  no current official app found (a
269	  [2010-era iPhone app](https://itwire.com/software/laugh-it-up-on-the-iphone-melbourne-international-comedy-festival-app.html)

343	### Leicester Comedy Festival — the UK's second clash problem, operator now dead
344	
345	The February anchor of UK comedy, and this pass's most dramatic finding:
346	**the organising charity collapsed in August 2026**, weeks before this page
347	was written.
348	
349	- **Shape**: open access — "anyone can pay a fee to put on an event",
350	  registered through Eventotron
351	  ([registration page](https://comedy-festival-takepart.co.uk/how-to-register-your-show))
352	  — annual each February since 1994, same city. 2026:
353	  [700+ shows across 81 venues](https://leicestertimes.com/leicester-news/leicester-comedy-festival-launches-with-over-700-shows-celebrating-the-art-of-comedy/52061/)
354	  over 19 days, plus a kids' comedy festival. Its own events API (fetched)
355	  counts 753 shows whose bookings average **2.28 days per show** — so the
356	  clash problem is fringe-scale (**242 shows on the peak Saturday**, per the
357	  API's date taxonomy) while the *runs* are short visits, not
358	  Edinburgh-length seasons. Venues run from a city-centre core out to county
359	  village halls.
360	- **Ticketing & data**: central box office on the festival's own site — the
361	  **Eventotron** WordPress plugin plus Stripe, leaving a fully open REST API
362	  (`events.comedy-festival.co.uk/wp-json/wp/v2/events`, 753 events with
363	  dates/genres/venues taxonomies, verified by fetch) — the same substrate
364	  and API shape as Brighton Fringe below: **one adapter would read both**.
365	- **The collapse**: operator Big Difference Company (charity 1135167) became
366	  insolvent and ceased trading —
367	  [its own 26 Aug 2026 statement](https://irp.cdn-website.com/b436dc39/files/uploaded/Statement+BDC+26_08_2026.docx)
368	  — with [debts over £215,000](https://www.chortle.co.uk/news/2026/08/22/61391/leicester_comedy_festival_charitys_debts_exceed_%c2%a3215,000)
369	  and performers owed their ticket money (the Feb 2026 festival *happened*;
370	  Wikipedia's "cancelled" lede is wrong). February 2027 is now contested:
371	  the [city council has pledged a successor festival](https://www.chortle.co.uk/news/2026/08/06/61209/leicester_mayor:_we_will_have_a_comedy_festival_next_year)
372	  (3–21 Feb 2027 per the old site's banner) while comedian Alex Hylton's
373	  [**Independent Comedy Festival**](https://www.chortle.co.uk/news/2026/08/11/61247/leicester_gets_a_new_comedy_festival)
374	  launches in the same window and venues — on **TixEvery**, a platform that
375	  pays comedians directly so the festival never holds box-office money (a
376	  ticketing model born directly of the collapse). For the product: the
377	  incumbent data source works today and its owner is in liquidation — which
378	  festival "is" Leicester next year is genuinely open.

407	## The showcase majors: dossiers
408	
409	Big festivals where the visitor picks headliners rather than solves a
410	schedule — one-night curated events, few or no repeats, tickets scattered
411	across vendors. The blunt cross-cutting finding from the US research: **no US
412	major is fringe-shaped.**
413	
414	### The Just For Laughs empire — survived receivership, showcase to the bone
415	
416	The census's nine JFL entries are one company plus its licensees, and its
417	recent history is the sharpest annual-vs-durable case in the circuit:
418	
419	- **The ownership arc**: founded 1983 (Gilbert Rozon); sold 2018 to the Howie
420	  Mandel / ICM / Bell Media / Groupe CH group after Rozon's resignation;
421	  **filed for creditor protection in March 2024** — the 2024 Montreal and
422	  Toronto festivals were cancelled outright, with
423	  [$22.5m of debt and an $800k loss to email phishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_for_Laughs)
424	  later revealed; assets acquired mid-2024 by **ComediHa!** (Sylvain
425	  Parent-Bédard's Quebec City group, per
426	  [CTV](https://www.ctvnews.ca/montreal/article/quebec-entertainment-group-comediha-confirms-acquisition-of-just-for-laughs-assets/)),
427	  parent since renamed Groupe Juste pour divertir. A reduced 2025 comeback,
428	  then a full-volume 2026: the
429	  [44th Montreal edition, 15–26 July — ~250 shows, ~25 venues, 800+ artists](https://www.themain.com/articles/just-for-laughs-montreal-2026-guide),
430	  with [2027 satellite dates already published](https://comedyevent.bm/).
431	  Read: a durable annual anchor again — two years into a turnaround, its
432	  scale figures its own marketing.
433	- **The Montreal model** is three tiers, none of them fringe runs: TV-taping
434	  **galas** at Place des Arts; **curated showcase runs of 1–5 nights** (The
435	  Nasty Show, Midnight Surprise) plus premium one-offs (Letterman at up to
436	  $550, per [Cult MTL](https://cultmtl.com/2026/07/just-for-laughs-and-off-jfl-are-showcasing-hundreds-of-great-comedians-in-montreal-from-july-15-to-26/));
437	  and a huge **free outdoor** programme at Place des Festivals.
438	  [Place des Arts' "nearly two million visitors"](https://www.placedesarts.com/en/festival/just-for-laughs-festival)
439	  counts those free crowds — which is how "world's largest comedy festival"
440	  survives as a label while MICF trebles its ticketed show count. The
441	  fringe-ish annex is **OFF-JPR** (the relaunched
442	  [Zoofest](https://www.offjpr.com/), ~one-night $24–32 club sets), and the
443	  industry layer is ComedyPRO with the New Faces showcases. Everything sits
444	  in the Quartier des Spectacles — concentrated, walkable, evening slots at
445	  7:00/9:30/midnight; a missed showcase usually repeats tomorrow, so clash
446	  pain is modest.
447	- **Franchise map**: Montreal, Quebec City (the rebranded 25-year-old
448	  ComediHa! Fest, now deliberately overlapping Montreal's dates), Toronto
449	  (ex-JFL42, relaunched 2025, [24 Sep–3 Oct 2026](https://toronto.hahaha.com/))
450	  and Vancouver ([12–22 Feb, 100+ shows](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/just-for-laughs-vancouver-2026))
451	  are owned-and-operated; Sydney and Singapore run with promoter Bohm
452	  Presents ([justforlaughs.sydney](https://www.justforlaughs.sydney/) is a
453	  tour-stop model on Opera House + external venue ticketing); Bermuda,
454	  Belgium (Namur) and Switzerland are local promoters carrying the brand.
455	  **The tracker's "JFL Paris" entry appears dead** — the hahaha.com festival
456	  URL 404s and no 2026 edition was found.
457	- **Ticketing & data**: the hahaha.com family sells on its **own platform**
458	  (a proprietary "Nova" CMS with Stripe, per-city baskets and a wishlist);
459	  Sydney explicitly fans out to six external sellers. No structured API; the
460	  programme loads as client-side HTML fragments — and **listings are
461	  ephemeral: city sites were emptied within weeks of the festival ending**,
462	  so any programme capture has to happen during the on-sale window.
463	- **Concurrents**: Montreal's window near-totally overlaps the
464	  [Fantasia film festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fantasia_International_Film_Festival)
465	  with Nuits d'Afrique brushing its first weekend — a real multi-festival
466	  cluster; Toronto's autumn slot dodges TIFF entirely.

468	### Netflix Is A Joke — maximum scale, biennial, and an anti-planner FAQ
469	
470	- **Biennial, not annual**: editions
471	  [2022, 2024, 2026 — no 2023 or 2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix_Is_a_Joke_Festival)
472	  (a resale SEO site wearing a 2025 name misleads searches). Corporate-run
473	  by Netflix; 4–10 May 2026 delivered.

475	  venues… the largest comedy event in history"; the schedule page's inlined
476	  dataset carries **498 dated events across 116 venue slugs**, peaking at
477	  **101 events on the Saturday** — numerically the hardest clash problem in
478	  US comedy, spread across greater LA from the Hollywood Bowl to the Intuit

480	  it as pick-your-headliner anyway.

483	  Ticketmaster 167, Eventbrite 118, ShowClix 51, TicketWeb 34, …).
484	- **Data**: paradoxically the easiest big scrape in the US — a Next.js site
485	  that **inlines the entire event dataset (1.4MB) in the server-rendered
486	  payload** of [/schedule](https://www.netflixisajokefest.com/schedule):
487	  per-event times, venue ids, ticket URLs, per-venue lat/long, capacity,

545	### The promoter slates and the rest, briefly
546	
547	- **[Nashville Comedy Festival](https://www.nashcomedyfest.com/)** and
548	  **[312 Comedy Festival](https://www.312comedyfestival.com/)** (Chicago)
549	  are both "presented by Outback Presents" — a promoter's April/November
550	  booking slate wearing a festival name: arena and theatre one-nighters plus
551	  club weekends, per-venue ticketing (Etix/AXS/Ticketmaster counted in the
552	  hundreds of links on their own pages). 312's Zanies club weekends — the
553	  same comic doing 2 shows a night for a weekend — are the nearest thing to
554	  a "run" in US club culture.
555	- **[Boston Comedy Festival](https://www.bostoncomedyfest.com/)** (26th
556	  year) is **competition-spined**: open submissions, ~96 comics through

558	  contest schedule.
559	- **[Skankfest](https://skankfest.com/)** (GaS Digital) is the
560	  **anti-planner**: one venue compound, pass-only (Tixr), 11am–midnight

562	  day of the festival"**. Fans buy the brand, not a lineup; sold out seven
563	  years running. Roving city history (Queens → Houston → Las Vegas → New
564	  Orleans).
565	- **[Del Close Marathon](https://ucbcomedy.com/)** (UCB, NYC): **56
566	  nonstop hours** of improv across six stages in two venues on a badge —

568	- **[NY Laughs Fest](https://nylaughsfest.com/)** (2nd year, nonprofit):
569	  free public-space comedy (Union Square) plus 20+ club shows — a civic

582	  entry links to what
583	  [redirects to dublincomedyfestival.ie](https://www.dublincomedyfestival.ie/),

590	  (Aiken Promotions, Iveagh Gardens, four days each July); September in

604	- **[Greenwich Comedy Garden](https://www.greenwichcomedygarden.co.uk/)** —
605	  tracker correction: rebranded from "Greenwich Comedy Festival" (the old

609	  **replicated single-site format**, the UK's polite cousin of the Great
610	  Outdoors model below.
611	- **[Roundhouse Comedy Festival](https://www.roundhouse.org.uk/seasons/roundhouse-comedy-festival/)**
612	  — tracker correction: 2026 actually ran **1–18 August** (not 23–26), one
613	  Camden building, curated with Berk's Nest, headline one-nighters and live
614	  podcasts on the venue's own box office — a single-building season that
615	  deliberately counter-programs the Edinburgh month.
616	- **[London Clown Festival](https://www.londonclownfest.online/)** (tracker's
617	  domain is dead; this is the live one) — niche curated clown/physical
618	  programme split between Soho Theatre and Jacksons Lane, each on its own
619	  box office. The census's 15-day length is two venues' seasons, not a
620	  dense festival.
621	
622	### Dubai Comedy Festival — the destination-marketing umbrella
623	
624	- **Organizer**: a government-backed promoter consortium — [BRAG "partnered
625	  with DTCM (Dubai's tourism department) and Live Nation to bring back the
626	  festival" in 2020](https://brag.world/dubai-comedy-festival); recent editions
627	  are presented by Dubai Calendar and produced by BRAG, Live Nation, GME
628	  Events and DXB Live (per [Katch International](https://katchinternational.com/)).
629	  Annual since the 2020 revival, 7th edition in 2026, grown from 4 days to 10.
630	- **Scale & model**: ["50+ artists, 40+ shows, 3+ venues"](https://www.dubaicomedyfest.ae/about)
631	  over 10 days — one-night international touring acts (Mo Gilligan, Katherine
632	  Ryan, Vir Das…), many "presented by" third-party promoters under the
633	  festival umbrella, deliberately multilingual (English, Arabic, Hindi, Urdu,
634	  Russian), plus a small up-and-comers sidebar ("Comedy Bizarre").
635	- **Venues & clash**: spread across a car-scale city — Dubai Opera, Coca-Cola
636	  Arena, Mall of the Emirates theatre, clubs; 2–3 shows per evening across
637	  distant venues. Lineup-picking with traffic, not a schedule grid.
638	- **Ticketing & data**: per-show, multi-vendor — mostly
639	  [Platinumlist](https://dubaicomedyfestival.platinumlist.net/) (which runs an
640	  aggregating microsite), plus venue box offices and Ticketmaster.ae for some
641	  shows. The [shows page](https://www.dubaicomedyfest.ae/shows) is
642	  server-rendered Squarespace carrying every show's date, venue, language,
643	  price and vendor link in plain HTML — the easiest large-festival page to
644	  read mechanically in the whole census.
645	
646	## The structural exhibits
647	
648	Festivals that mark out the edges of the taxonomy — none is a planner market,
649	and each pins down one shape the census keeps producing.
650	
651	### Great Outdoors Comedy Festival — the music-festival pole, confirmed
652	
653	The hypothesis the census raised, confirmed and then some: GOCF is not even a
654	serial tour but a **franchise running parallel one-stage city productions on
655	shared weekends** — [seven 2026 stops](https://greatoutdoorscomedyfestival.com/):
656	Edmonton *and* Winnipeg both 17–19 July, Calgary *and* Vancouver 28–30 August
657	with Spokane the same weekend, Halifax 6–9 August, Mississauga 11–13
658	September; 2027 dates already on sale. Owned and run by
659	[Trixstar](https://greatoutdoorscomedyfestival.com/about), an Edmonton
660	promoter; since 2021 it claims 400,000+ cumulative attendees. One outdoor
661	stage per city (Vancouver's Stanley Park permit caps at
662	[10,000/day](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/the-great-outdoors-comedy-festival-proposal-stanley-park)),
663	two shows a day (matinee + evening), each a one-off bill of touring headliners
664	(Bill Burr, Matt Rife, Pete Davidson tiers), grounds cleared between shows,
665	explicitly [no application process](https://greatoutdoorscomedyfestival.com/gocf-faqs)
666	for performers, GA/VIP tiers, no re-entry, 18+/19+. Ticketing is
667	[Tixr-only](https://greatoutdoorscomedyfestival.com/cities/vancouver); the
668	Webflow site is fully server-rendered. **Scheduling problem: none by design —
669	the only decision is which city you are in.** This is what "comedy festival"
670	means when the shape is literally a music festival's.
671	
672	### The TV-taping festivals — Winnipeg and Halifax
673	
674	Canada's two legacy festivals are shaped end to end by broadcast production,
675	and they show what a "festival" is when its real product is television:
676	
677	- **[Winnipeg Comedy Festival](https://www.winnipegcomedyfestival.com/about-us)**
678	  (annual since 2002, produced by the nonprofit Gas Station Arts Centre):
679	  ["30+ shows. 9 venues. 85 comics"](https://www.winnipegcomedyfestival.com/news/post/105)
680	  over 7 days, anchored by five "Mega Shows" **recorded for CBC** at the
681	  Burton Cummings Theatre — celebrity host + six comics, PG while cameras
682	  roll, in a venue chosen for camera/crew needs (which forces Ticketmaster;
683	  everything else sells through local ticketer 3Common, per
684	  [its FAQ](https://www.winnipegcomedyfestival.com/faqs)). The broadcast
685	  audience ("over 2 million viewers annually — CBC Television's highest-rated
686	  comedy festival series") dwarfs the live one. 2–3 parallel rooms at peak;
687	  lineup-picking.
688	- **[Halifax ComedyFest](https://www.halifaxcomedyfest.ca/about-the-fest.html)**
689	  (annual since 1995): self-described as "one of only three major comedy
690	  festivals broadcast nationally in prime time on CBC Television… as a
691	  six-episode series"; [its application page](https://www.halifaxcomedyfest.ca/apply.html)
692	  demands "corporate clean" audition tapes and caps international bookings

[Resource from github at repo://missingbulb/edfringenow/sha/35005df09923192ba459e03049a83516cbab2708/contents/product-wiki/festival-circuits/README.md] # The festival circuits

The world's comedy festivals as a market: what exists, what shape each one is,
and what it would take to point EdFringeNow's planning product at any of them.
This page exists because the owner's direction (2026-09-01) is to grow
EdFringeNow into a festival-planning product, and the first expansion axis is
the art form the product already serves best — comedy is the Fringe's largest
genre. Compiled once, refined in place.

Division of labour with the neighbouring pages:
[festmaxxing-environments/](../festmaxxing-environments/README.md)
owns the *city* question (which cities carry the Edinburgh-in-August overwhelm
pattern, whatever the art form); this page owns the *comedy festival* question —
the worldwide circuit, each festival's structure, organizer, ticketing and data
reachability — plus a deliberately light survey of the **film** festivals that
share the planner-complex shape (its own section below). Planner-type
competitors found along the way live on
[competitor-landscape/](../competitor-landscape/README.md).

## Key insights

- Only ~8 of 85 census festivals are fringe-shaped. Most of the circuit is one-night showcases with nothing to schedule.
- MICF is the southern Edinburgh — 803 shows, 9,164 performances, open registration — with unauthenticated JSON APIs.
- Leicester's operator went bust in Aug 2026 owing performers ticket money. Feb 2027 is two rival reboots.
- Nearly everything is annual in the same city, but brands churn: JFL survived receivership, Netflix Is A Joke is biennial.
- Recurrence decides planning — in film too: Fringe shows play ~14 times, Berlinale screens films up to 5×, US one-offs are terminal.
- Leicester and Brighton share one platform (Eventotron) and identical open APIs — one adapter reads both.
- No machine-readable comedy-festival calendar exists. The best tracker is one journalist's hand-kept page.

## The census: a year of comedy festivals

The seed source is the festival tracker kept by From The Comic's Comic
([fromthecomicscomic.com/comedy-festivals/](https://fromthecomicscomic.com/comedy-festivals/),
fetched 2026-09-01), which lists the circuit by month for 2026 with a stated
confirmation policy — "If it's not listed, it's not confirmed yet." The full
2026 list, with run lengths computed from its dates:

Not in the table: three undated entries — the **San Francisco Comedy
Competition** ("across the Bay Area") and **Seattle International Comedy
Competition** ("all month across Western Washington", November), both
month-long *touring competitions* rather than city takeovers, and **Just For
Laughs Singapore** (tbd) — plus the first 2027 confirmations (JFL Bermuda,
17–20 Feb 2027; SXSW, 17–20 Mar 2027). The tracker's own dates are treated
here as launch-time claims, not delivered totals — and the dossiers below
correct five of its entries against primary sources: Roundhouse actually ran
1–18 Aug, Greenwich has rebranded to "Comedy Garden", the "Dublin Comedy
Festival" is a suburban pub circuit, JFL Paris appears dead, and
Machynlleth (the UK's best small-town takeover) is missing entirely.

What the census says before any per-festival research:

- **The circuit is mostly weekend showcases.** 45 of 85 dated festivals run ≤4
  days, and 56 of 85 are in the US — overwhelmingly club-scale, curated or
  submission-based weekends where a visitor picks a headliner, not a schedule.
- **The fringe-length tier is small and un-American.** Only 13 festivals run
  ≥14 days, and the US contributes just two (SF Sketchfest and the new Fallout
  Fringe in Las Vegas); the other eleven are UK, Irish, Australian and NZ
  events — Edinburgh, Adelaide, Brighton, Melbourne, Sydney Comedy Festival,
  JFL Sydney, NZICF, Leicester, Aberdeen, the London Clown Festival, and the
  Dublin entry examined below.
- **Run length is a strong first classifier.** A festival long enough to need
  repeat performances of the same show is where a scheduling product has work
  to do; a weekend of one-night showcases is not. The dossiers below test that
  presumption festival by festival.

## The two shapes, and what decides planner-worthiness

The owner's framing question — which festivals behave like the Fringe and
which like music festivals — turns out to rest on two measurable axes, and
the dossiers below supply the numbers:

1. **Parallel volume**: how many shows run at once. Edinburgh peaks in the
   thousands per day; MICF at ~350; Leicester's own API shows 242 on its
   peak Saturday; Netflix Is A Joke ~100; Sydney ~29; most of the census
   runs single digits. Below a few dozen parallel shows, "which can I make"
   stops being a problem a product needs to solve.
2. **Recurrence**: how many times one show plays. Edinburgh averages ~14
   performances per show and MICF ~11 — miss tonight, catch tomorrow, so
   planning is *packing*. Sydney averages 2.4 and Leicester 2.28; the US
   majors run one-night events almost exclusively — every clash is
   terminal, so planning is *triage*, and with few parallel shows it
   reduces to picking headliners.

Two more axes modulate the answer: **venue geography** (a walkable core —
Edinburgh, MICF's CBD, Machynlleth — makes multi-show days physically
possible; a car city like LA or Dubai caps a day at one neighbourhood;
a single site has nothing to route) and **access model** (open access —
anyone who pays registers — is what produces uncapped supply; curation caps
it by construction).

The resulting map of the census:

- **Fringe-shaped** (open access, repeated runs, many venues, real clash
  grid): Edinburgh, Adelaide, **MICF**, **Brighton** (46% comedy), and
  **Leicester** in its short-visit variant — plus **NZICF** small and
  **Machynlleth** miniature. This is the entire planner-market tier, and
  outside Edinburgh none of it has a third-party planner
  ([competitor-landscape/](../competitor-landscape/README.md)).
- **Showcase-shaped** (curated one-nighters, pick-your-headliner): the JFL
  empire, NYCF, Sydney, Perth, Galway, Dubai, Aberdeen, Winnipeg, Halifax,
  Nashville, 312, and — at fringe *breadth* but one-off depth — SF
  Sketchfest and Netflix Is A Joke, where the planning problem is real but
  is scarcity-triage (nothing repeats) rather than schedule-packing.
- **Distinct sub-shapes the two poles don't cover**: the **badge-graze**
  festivals (Moontower's club binge, Del Close Marathon, SXSW) where entry
  is walk-in and the constraint is room capacity, not tickets; the
  **roving franchise** (Great Outdoors; 57 Festivals' Comedy Gardens) — one
  stage, touring cities; the **anti-planner compound** (Skankfest, schedule
  released day-of); the **touring competitions** (Boston's bracket, SF and
  Seattle's month-long circuits); the **TV-taping festivals** (Winnipeg,
  Halifax — the broadcast is the product); the **venue season** (Aberdeen,
  Roundhouse); the **club hub** (Tokyo, Grindstone); and the **pub circuit**
  wearing a festival name (the "Dublin Comedy Festival").

The product read: **run length in the census predicts the shape but does
not decide it** — Sydney (35 days) and Aberdeen (16) are showcases, while
Machynlleth (3 days) has a denser grid than either. The deciding pair is
parallel volume × recurrence, and only the fringe-shaped tier scores high
on both.

## The fringe-shaped tier: dossiers

The festivals where "which of tonight's shows can I make" is a real problem —
long runs, repeated performances, many parallel rooms. This is the tier a
planning product can serve.

### Melbourne International Comedy Festival — the southern Edinburgh

The standout of the whole census, and the closest thing to a second Edinburgh
Fringe anywhere in comedy.

- **Scale, delivered 2026** (the festival's own
  [40th-year wrap](https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/news/celebrating-a-record-40th-year/)):
  **803 shows and events, 9,164 performances, 26 days** (25 Mar–19 Apr),
  796,975 attendees (+13% YoY), A$26.6m box office, average paid ticket
  A$38.20. That is ~350 performances a day — genuinely fringe-like clash
  density. Launch press said "over 750 shows", so ~50 more landed after
  launch: the launch-undercount trap
  [edinburgh-market-and-audience/](../edinburgh-market-and-audience/README.md) documents holds
  here too.
- **Show model**: Edinburgh-style seasons — one show is the same hour repeated
  across the run (sampled runs of 7–24 performances; cheaper previews,
  cheap-Tuesday flags). Participation is **open registration**
  ([registrations open each October](https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/participate/),
  with independent venues found via a venue finder) — the Fringe's
  open-access mechanism, at ~one-fifth Edinburgh's scale.
- **Organizer & recurrence**: its own festival organization, annual every
  autumn since 1987, always Melbourne, centred on Melbourne Town Hall;
  [self-described](https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/about-us/) as "one of
  the three largest comedy festivals in the world, alongside Edinburgh
  Festival Fringe and Montreal's Just for Laughs" and "Australia's largest
  ticketed cultural event". Stable through a 2026 leadership handover
  (Susan Provan retired after 32 years;
  [Dylan Cole appointed CEO/Festival Director](https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/news/melbourne-international-comedy-festival-appoints-dylan-cole-as-new-ceofestival-director/)).
  2027 dates already announced (24 Mar–18 Apr).
- **Venues**: 143 venue buildings in its own venues data — 66 in the CBD, the
  rest a suburban tail (Northcote, Box Hill…) — a walkable core plus
  outliers, the Edinburgh pattern loosened one notch.
- **Ticketing**: comedyfestival.com.au is **its own central box office** with
  one basket across shows (a cart API, accounts, native favourites with
  share-a-favourites-list); a minority of external-venue shows link out to
  Ticketmaster/Ticketek/Arts Centre Melbourne.
- **Data reachability — best in the census**: unauthenticated JSON endpoints,
  verified by fetch:
  `POST /umbraco/api/searchapi/searchShows` (826 show records for 2026, paged,
  with runs, performance counts, venue rooms),
  `GET /umbraco/api/venuesapi/getvenues` (all 143 venues with address,
  capacity, accessibility flags), and each show page embeds a `sessionData`
  JSON array with per-performance date, time, **on-sale status and
  sold-out/preview/cheap-night flags** — near enough 1:1 onto the fields the
  Edinburgh scraper already produces. A
  [sitemap](https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/sitemap.xml) lists every show
  URL.
- **Concurrent**: Melbourne Food & Wine Festival and the Flower & Garden Show
  overlap the window, with the AFL season running throughout (per
  [melbournetourism.org](https://www.melbournetourism.org/melbourne-events-and-festivals-calendar/))
  — city-draw amplifiers, though nothing on the scale of Edinburgh's August
  cluster.
- **Planner field**: the site's account favourites are the only planning tool;
  no current official app found (a
  [2010-era iPhone app](https://itwire.com/software/laugh-it-up-on-the-iphone-melbourne-international-comedy-festival-app.html)
  is the last trace), and no third-party planner exists — see
  [competitor-landscape/](../competitor-landscape/README.md).

### Adelaide Fringe — covered elsewhere, plus the ticketing angle

Scale, open access and the "Mad March" cluster are on
[festmaxxing-environments/](../festmaxxing-environments/README.md);
what this pass adds is ticketing and data. Adelaide Fringe Inc. (a
not-for-profit, incorporated 1975) runs **its own ticketing platform,
FringeTIX** — [first used in 1998](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide_Fringe),
today a Rails app inside adelaidefringe.com.au with a central cart across all
shows and venues — and [markets that platform (AVR) to other open-access
festivals](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/about-us) as "the best solution for
collating and managing open access festivals". No public API was found
(probes 404/500 off-season); a scrape would target the server-rendered
FringeTIX listing in season. Comedy's share of the ~1,500-show programme is
not published —
[the 2026 launch](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/fringefeed/news/2026-program-unveiled-with-more-than-1500-shows)
lists comedy first among genres with no counts.

### NZ International Comedy Festival — one festival, two cities at once

- **Organizer**: the [New Zealand Comedy Trust](https://comedyfestival.co.nz/about-us/the-new-zealand-comedy-trust/),
  a charitable not-for-profit; festival annual each May since 1995 (roots
  1993), 2026 = the 33rd Auckland edition and the Wellington leg's 30th.
- **The two-city model**: one programme, one window (1–24 May 2026), running
  **simultaneously** in Auckland and Wellington with region-filtered listings
  (plus a "Gala toe-dip" in Christchurch in 2026); some acts play a season in
  each city inside the window. Each city is a compact centre cluster
  (Auckland: Q Theatre, Basement, The Classic + big halls for headliners;
  Wellington: BATS' three rooms, Te Auaha, Hannah Playhouse).
- **Scale & model**: the Trust's steady-state description is
  ["over 120 show seasons, over 600 performances, around 200 comedians"](https://comedyfestival.co.nz/about-us/new-zealand-international-comedy-festival/),
  75,000+ attendance in 2025 — Edinburgh-style short seasons (~5 performances
  each), a real but small evening-choice problem (~a dozen parallel shows per
  city on peak nights).
- **Ticketing**: **no central basket** — the festival site is a catalogue that
  [hands buyers to the right agent per show](https://comedyfestival.co.nz/how-to-buy-tickets):
  Ticketmaster, Q Theatre's box office, Eventfinda or iTicket, each with its
  own fees. A cross-show plan means juggling up to four seller accounts.
- **Data**: server-rendered SilverStripe site, no JSON API found; a scrape
  targets the find-a-show HTML per region.
- **Concurrent**: May in Auckland is genuinely congested — NZ Music Month plus
  the Auckland Writers Festival inside the window;
  [The Spinoff](https://thespinoff.co.nz/pop-culture/06-05-2026/auckland-has-a-problem-everything-awesome-is-happening-in-may-all-at-once):
  "Auckland has a problem. Everything awesome is happening in May, all at
  once."
- **Planner field**: the official planning tool is a downloadable timetable
  PDF. Nothing else exists.

### Sydney Comedy Festival — the boundary case

Fringe-scale show count, showcase-shaped mechanics — the census's clearest
demonstration that show count alone doesn't decide the shape:

- **Delivered 2026** (per the festival's wrap, carried by
  [The Movie Boards](https://www.themovieboards.net/2026/05/18/record-growth-and-huge-crowds-for-sydney-comedy-festival/)):
  **411 shows, close to 1,000 performances, 57 venues, 175,000+ attendees**
  over 35 days (13 Apr–17 May) — but that is **~2.4 performances per show**
  against MICF's ~11.4: mostly weekend-length visits, galas and showcases,
  not month-long seasons.
- **Structure**: run by [Century Entertainment](https://www.century.com.au/about/),
  a commercial venue group (Enmore Theatre, Comedy Store…), **curated by
  application**, venues scattered "from Bondi to Penrith" (a metro
  constellation, not a walkable core), **per-venue ticketing** with no
  central basket (Century venues on TicketSearch, tour venues on their own
  sellers), followed by a national showcase tour May–December. Concurrent:
  Sydney Royal Easter Show and Writers' Festival brush the window, Vivid
  starts just after.
- Century also produces the **[Perth Comedy Festival](https://www.perthcomedyfestival.com/about/)**
  (20 Apr–17 May 2026, ~70 gigs across 5 venues — fully showcase-shaped) on
  the same WordPress codebase — one scrape adapter would cover both.

### Leicester Comedy Festival — the UK's second clash problem, operator now dead

The February anchor of UK comedy, and this pass's most dramatic finding:
**the organising charity collapsed in August 2026**, weeks before this page
was written.

- **Shape**: open access — "anyone can pay a fee to put on an event",
  registered through Eventotron
  ([registration page](https://comedy-festival-takepart.co.uk/how-to-register-your-show))
  — annual each February since 1994, same city. 2026:
  [700+ shows across 81 venues](https://leicestertimes.com/leicester-news/leicester-comedy-festival-launches-with-over-700-shows-celebrating-the-art-of-comedy/52061/)
  over 19 days, plus a kids' comedy festival. Its own events API (fetched)
  counts 753 shows whose bookings average **2.28 days per show** — so the
  clash problem is fringe-scale (**242 shows on the peak Saturday**, per the
  API's date taxonomy) while the *runs* are short visits, not
  Edinburgh-length seasons. Venues run from a city-centre core out to county
  village halls.
- **Ticketing & data**: central box office on the festival's own site — the
  **Eventotron** WordPress plugin plus Stripe, leaving a fully open REST API
  (`events.comedy-festival.co.uk/wp-json/wp/v2/events`, 753 events with
  dates/genres/venues taxonomies, verified by fetch) — the same substrate
  and API shape as Brighton Fringe below: **one adapter would read both**.
- **The collapse**: operator Big Difference Company (charity 1135167) became
  insolvent and ceased trading —
  [its own 26 Aug 2026 statement](https://irp.cdn-website.com/b436dc39/files/uploaded/Statement+BDC+26_08_2026.docx)
  — with [debts over £215,000](https://www.chortle.co.uk/news/2026/08/22/61391/leicester_comedy_festival_charitys_debts_exceed_%c2%a3215,000)
  and performers owed their ticket money (the Feb 2026 festival *happened*;
  Wikipedia's "cancelled" lede is wrong). February 2027 is now contested:
  the [city council has pledged a successor festival](https://www.chortle.co.uk/news/2026/08/06/61209/leicester_mayor:_we_will_have_a_comedy_festival_next_year)
  (3–21 Feb 2027 per the old site's banner) while comedian Alex Hylton's
  [**Independent Comedy Festival**](https://www.chortle.co.uk/news/2026/08/11/61247/leicester_gets_a_new_comedy_festival)
  launches in the same window and venues — on **TixEvery**, a platform that
  pays comedians directly so the festival never holds box-office money (a
  ticketing model born directly of the collapse). For the product: the
  incumbent data source works today and its owner is in liquidation — which
  festival "is" Leicester next year is genuinely open.

### Brighton Fringe — half of it is a comedy festival

Already profiled as a city on
[festmaxxing-environments/](../festmaxxing-environments/README.md);
what this pass adds is measured comedy share, mechanics and the cluster.
**Comedy is 46% of the live programme** — 394 of 864 events in its own
events API carry the Comedy genre (fetched; cross-edition genre totals give
42%) — making open-access, month-long Brighton effectively half a comedy
festival, the largest comedy event in the UK after Edinburgh with Leicester
gone. Central box office on brightonfringe.org itself, on the **same
Eventotron + Stripe substrate as Leicester** with the same open REST API
(the what's-on grid is client-rendered, but the API is not). Its May window
contains a real cluster:
[Brighton Festival (curated, 105 events, 1–25 May)](https://brightonfestival.org/press-office/press-release-brighton-festival-2026-launch/)
and [The Great Escape new-music showcase (13–16 May, 30+ venues)](https://www.livenation.co.uk/event/the-great-escape-2026-brighton-tickets-edp1637482)
sit wholly inside Brighton Fringe's 1–31 May.

### Machynlleth — the small-town takeover (missing from the tracker)

[Machynlleth Comedy Festival](https://machcomedyfest.co.uk/) is not on the
seed tracker at all and belongs in the census: run by producer Little
Wander, 15th year in 2026, **200+ shows in three days (1–3 May) in a Welsh
town of ~2,000 people** — ~65+ parallel-ish shows a day, a genuine clash
problem at miniature scale, with an official festival app. Single-curator
in structure, fringe-dense in feel: the reference point for the
"small-town takeover" model (Wells is its curated-weekend little sibling).

## The showcase majors: dossiers

Big festivals where the visitor picks headliners rather than solves a
schedule — one-night curated events, few or no repeats, tickets scattered
across vendors. The blunt cross-cutting finding from the US research: **no US
major is fringe-shaped.**

### The Just For Laughs empire — survived receivership, showcase to the bone

The census's nine JFL entries are one company plus its licensees, and its
recent history is the sharpest annual-vs-durable case in the circuit:

- **The ownership arc**: founded 1983 (Gilbert Rozon); sold 2018 to the Howie
  Mandel / ICM / Bell Media / Groupe CH group after Rozon's resignation;
  **filed for creditor protection in March 2024** — the 2024 Montreal and
  Toronto festivals were cancelled outright, with
  [$22.5m of debt and an $800k loss to email phishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_for_Laughs)
  later revealed; assets acquired mid-2024 by **ComediHa!** (Sylvain
  Parent-Bédard's Quebec City group, per
  [CTV](https://www.ctvnews.ca/montreal/article/quebec-entertainment-group-comediha-confirms-acquisition-of-just-for-laughs-assets/)),
  parent since renamed Groupe Juste pour divertir. A reduced 2025 comeback,
  then a full-volume 2026: the
  [44th Montreal edition, 15–26 July — ~250 shows, ~25 venues, 800+ artists](https://www.themain.com/articles/just-for-laughs-montreal-2026-guide),
  with [2027 satellite dates already published](https://comedyevent.bm/).
  Read: a durable annual anchor again — two years into a turnaround, its
  scale figures its own marketing.
- **The Montreal model** is three tiers, none of them fringe runs: TV-taping
  **galas** at Place des Arts; **curated showcase runs of 1–5 nights** (The
  Nasty Show, Midnight Surprise) plus premium one-offs (Letterman at up to
  $550, per [Cult MTL](https://cultmtl.com/2026/07/just-for-laughs-and-off-jfl-are-showcasing-hundreds-of-great-comedians-in-montreal-from-july-15-to-26/));
  and a huge **free outdoor** programme at Place des Festivals.
  [Place des Arts' "nearly two million visitors"](https://www.placedesarts.com/en/festival/just-for-laughs-festival)
  counts those free crowds — which is how "world's largest comedy festival"
  survives as a label while MICF trebles its ticketed show count. The
  fringe-ish annex is **OFF-JPR** (the relaunched
  [Zoofest](https://www.offjpr.com/), ~one-night $24–32 club sets), and the
  industry layer is ComedyPRO with the New Faces showcases. Everything sits
  in the Quartier des Spectacles — concentrated, walkable, evening slots at
  7:00/9:30/midnight; a missed showcase usually repeats tomorrow, so clash
  pain is modest.
- **Franchise map**: Montreal, Quebec City (the rebranded 25-year-old
  ComediHa! Fest, now deliberately overlapping Montreal's dates), Toronto
  (ex-JFL42, relaunched 2025, [24 Sep–3 Oct 2026](https://toronto.hahaha.com/))
  and Vancouver ([12–22 Feb, 100+ shows](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/just-for-laughs-vancouver-2026))
  are owned-and-operated; Sydney and Singapore run with promoter Bohm
  Presents ([justforlaughs.sydney](https://www.justforlaughs.sydney/) is a
  tour-stop model on Opera House + external venue ticketing); Bermuda,
  Belgium (Namur) and Switzerland are local promoters carrying the brand.
  **The tracker's "JFL Paris" entry appears dead** — the hahaha.com festival
  URL 404s and no 2026 edition was found.
- **Ticketing & data**: the hahaha.com family sells on its **own platform**
  (a proprietary "Nova" CMS with Stripe, per-city baskets and a wishlist);
  Sydney explicitly fans out to six external sellers. No structured API; the
  programme loads as client-side HTML fragments — and **listings are
  ephemeral: city sites were emptied within weeks of the festival ending**,
  so any programme capture has to happen during the on-sale window.
- **Concurrents**: Montreal's window near-totally overlaps the
  [Fantasia film festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fantasia_International_Film_Festival)
  with Nuits d'Afrique brushing its first weekend — a real multi-festival
  cluster; Toronto's autumn slot dodges TIFF entirely.

### Netflix Is A Joke — maximum scale, biennial, and an anti-planner FAQ

- **Biennial, not annual**: editions
  [2022, 2024, 2026 — no 2023 or 2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix_Is_a_Joke_Festival)
  (a resale SEO site wearing a 2025 name misleads searches). Corporate-run
  by Netflix; 4–10 May 2026 delivered.
- **Scale**: its own site banner claims "475+ shows, 500+ artists, 45+
  venues… the largest comedy event in history"; the schedule page's inlined
  dataset carries **498 dated events across 116 venue slugs**, peaking at
  **101 events on the Saturday** — numerically the hardest clash problem in
  US comedy, spread across greater LA from the Hollywood Bowl to the Intuit
  Dome, where cross-town same-night stacking is impractical. Attendees treat
  it as pick-your-headliner anyway.
- **Ticketing**: the FAQ is explicit — "there are no festival passes"; 498
  events fan out to **12+ vendors** (counted from its own payload:
  Ticketmaster 167, Eventbrite 118, ShowClix 51, TicketWeb 34, …).
- **Data**: paradoxically the easiest big scrape in the US — a Next.js site
  that **inlines the entire event dataset (1.4MB) in the server-rendered
  payload** of [/schedule](https://www.netflixisajokefest.com/schedule):
  per-event times, venue ids, ticket URLs, per-venue lat/long, capacity,
  even parking and bag policy. One HTML fetch gives everything.
- **Planner field**: no official app; the site's favourites are the only
  tool, and no third party exists.

### SF Sketchfest — fringe breadth, one-off depth

[Founded 2001 and still run by its three founders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SF_Sketchfest);
annual each Jan/Feb (a COVID gap 2021–22), 23rd edition in 2026: **200+
shows, 500+ performers, 13 venues, 18 days** (per
[Deadline](https://deadline.com/)). The catch that decides its shape: the
programming is **reunions, tributes and one-night specials that structurally
cannot repeat** (a *Brain Candy* 30th anniversary, "The Women of SNL") — ~11
shows/day of unresolvable clashes, since nothing gets a second chance.
Tickets per show via a single
[Eventbrite organizer account](https://www.eventbrite.com/o/sf-sketchfest-57967098043);
planning outsourced to a yearly [Sched instance](https://sfsketchfest2026.sched.com/);
the festival's own site is bot-walled (SiteGround captcha), making Eventbrite
the practical machine surface.

### Moontower — the US festival with a fringe inside it

Run by the nonprofit [Paramount Theatre](https://www.austintheatre.org/moontower-comedy/)
(Austin Theatre Alliance) each April since 2012. Two tiers: two weeks of
theatre headliners on single tickets (Tessitura, the venue's own system) —
and the **4-day Club Binge**, where a **badge is walk-in access to 10+
walkable downtown clubs, no tickets or reservations**, 100+ comedians
playing multiple showcase slots. That binge is genuine fringe mechanics
(turn-up-and-graze, room-capacity risk instead of ticket clashes) — the
closest any US major comes. Note the census-table caveat: the "12 days"
overstates the fringe-like part; the binge is four.

### SXSW Comedy — a garnish on a badge mega-festival

[Since 2008](https://sxsw.com/festivals/comedy/), but tiny: the official
stats block for 2027 says **"4 nights, 2 venues, 65+ performers, 30 shows"**
— all included with an SXSW badge ($550–$1,395 tiers), no per-show tickets.
Comedy barely clashes with itself; it clashes with the 1,000+ music
showcases, film premieres and conference tracks on the same credential — the
purest "the city is the draw" case in the census, and the reason SXSW ships
the circuit's best official planner
([SXSW GO on Eventbase](https://www.eventbase.com/sxsw-go) + schedule.sxsw.com).

### New York Comedy Festival, and the November pile-up

[Founded 2004 by Caroline Hirsch and still produced by Carolines / 550
Comedy Inc.](https://nycomedyfestival.com/faq/) — "10 days, 5 boroughs,
100+ shows, 200+ comedians" grown to 150+ by August: headliner one-nighters
(Beacon, Town Hall, Kings Theatre, a Stand Up for Heroes gala) over ~39
venues with **per-venue ticketing** (Ticketmaster / ATG / house systems) and
open submissions confined to three contest-style showcases. Data note: a
live WordPress REST API
([/wp-json/wp/v2/lineup](https://nycomedyfestival.com/wp-json/wp/v2/lineup?per_page=2))
makes it scrapable without a browser. Its window sits in the **US November
pile-up**: NYCF (6–15), 312 Chicago (5–15), Boston (10–14) and Skankfest
New Orleans (13–15) all overlap, circulating the same touring headliners
through different cities.

### The promoter slates and the rest, briefly

- **[Nashville Comedy Festival](https://www.nashcomedyfest.com/)** and
  **[312 Comedy Festival](https://www.312comedyfestival.com/)** (Chicago)
  are both "presented by Outback Presents" — a promoter's April/November
  booking slate wearing a festival name: arena and theatre one-nighters plus
  club weekends, per-venue ticketing (Etix/AXS/Ticketmaster counted in the
  hundreds of links on their own pages). 312's Zanies club weekends — the
  same comic doing 2 shows a night for a weekend — are the nearest thing to
  a "run" in US club culture.
- **[Boston Comedy Festival](https://www.bostoncomedyfest.com/)** (26th
  year) is **competition-spined**: open submissions, ~96 comics through
  bracket rounds to a Somerville Theatre final — fringe-adjacent spirit,
  contest schedule.
- **[Skankfest](https://skankfest.com/)** (GaS Digital) is the
  **anti-planner**: one venue compound, pass-only (Tixr), 11am–midnight
  overlapping sets — and **"the full festival schedule will be released the
  day of the festival"**. Fans buy the brand, not a lineup; sold out seven
  years running. Roving city history (Queens → Houston → Las Vegas → New
  Orleans).
- **[Del Close Marathon](https://ucbcomedy.com/)** (UCB, NYC): **56
  nonstop hours** of improv across six stages in two venues on a badge —
  round-the-clock grazing, structurally one continuous show.
- **[NY Laughs Fest](https://nylaughsfest.com/)** (2nd year, nonprofit):
  free public-space comedy (Union Square) plus 20+ club shows — a civic
  showcase.

### The UK & Ireland showcase belt, briefly

- **[Galway Comedy Festival](https://galwaycomedyfestival.ie/)** — "Ireland's
  largest comedy festival" by its own meta description, ex-"Vodafone Comedy
  Carnival": a curated headliner week each October
  ([69 shows / 16 venues in 2025, per RTÉ](https://www.rte.ie/culture/2025/0911/1533013-galway-comedy-festival-reveals-2025-line-up-ahead-of-october-bash/)),
  grown out of the Róisín Dubh venue, ~10 shows/day. Self-run ticketing on a
  custom SPA built with Base44 (an AI app-builder) — which also exposes its
  operator admin routes in the page shell.
- **The "Dublin Comedy Festival" untangled** — the tracker's 23-day September
  entry links to what
  [redirects to dublincomedyfestival.ie](https://www.dublincomedyfestival.ie/),
  whose own headline is "**West Dublin's Comedy Takeover**": ~20 shows of the
  same few acts rotating suburban pubs and hotels (Reginald D Hunter ×4
  nights), per-event tickets on Universe. It is a rebranded pub circuit, not
  a fringe — the census's second-longest UK entry dissolves on inspection.
  Dublin's real big comedy event is the
  [Paddy Power Comedy Festival](https://aikenpromotions.com/show/paddy-power-comedy-festival/)
  (Aiken Promotions, Iveagh Gardens, four days each July); September in
  Dublin belongs to the theatre-led
  [Dublin Fringe](https://www.fringefest.com/news/dublin-fringe-festival) —
  the likely source of the label confusion.
- **[Aberdeen Comedy Festival](https://www.aberdeenperformingarts.com/aberdeen-comedy-festival/)**
  — the venue-trust model: Aberdeen Performing Arts (the charity running the
  Music Hall, His Majesty's and The Lemon Tree) programmes a curated
  three-weekend season (19 Sep–4 Oct 2026, Russell Howard, Susan Calman) on
  its own Spektrix box office. A handful of shows a night; no clash problem.
  The census's 16-day length flatters it — it is three weekends, not a run.
- **[Wells Comedy Festival](https://www.wellscomfest.com/)** — the curated
  small-town weekend: produced by Plosive (the podcast company), 10th
  edition 2026, three walkable rooms in England's smallest city, big-name
  bills (Acaster, Pascoe, Kumar), TicketSource ticketing.
- **[Greenwich Comedy Garden](https://www.greenwichcomedygarden.co.uk/)** —
  tracker correction: rebranded from "Greenwich Comedy Festival" (the old
  domain redirects). Producer 57 Festivals' five-night big-top residency at
  the Old Royal Naval College — mixed-bill headliner nights, See Tickets —
  and the same team runs Brighton/Cambridge/Norwich Comedy Gardens: a
  **replicated single-site format**, the UK's polite cousin of the Great
  Outdoors model below.
- **[Roundhouse Comedy Festival](https://www.roundhouse.org.uk/seasons/roundhouse-comedy-festival/)**
  — tracker correction: 2026 actually ran **1–18 August** (not 23–26), one
  Camden building, curated with Berk's Nest, headline one-nighters and live
  podcasts on the venue's own box office — a single-building season that
  deliberately counter-programs the Edinburgh month.
- **[London Clown Festival](https://www.londonclownfest.online/)** (tracker's
  domain is dead; this is the live one) — niche curated clown/physical
  programme split between Soho Theatre and Jacksons Lane, each on its own
  box office. The census's 15-day length is two venues' seasons, not a
  dense festival.

### Dubai Comedy Festival — the destination-marketing umbrella

- **Organizer**: a government-backed promoter consortium — [BRAG "partnered
  with DTCM (Dubai's tourism department) and Live Nation to bring back the
  festival" in 2020](https://brag.world/dubai-comedy-festival); recent editions
  are presented by Dubai Calendar and produced by BRAG, Live Nation, GME
  Events and DXB Live (per [Katch International](https://katchinternational.com/)).
  Annual since the 2020 revival, 7th edition in 2026, grown from 4 days to 10.
- **Scale & model**: ["50+ artists, 40+ shows, 3+ venues"](https://www.dubaicomedyfest.ae/about)
  over 10 days — one-night international touring acts (Mo Gilligan, Katherine
  Ryan, Vir Das…), many "presented by" third-party promoters under the
  festival umbrella, deliberately multilingual (English, Arabic, Hindi, Urdu,
  Russian), plus a small up-and-comers sidebar ("Comedy Bizarre").
- **Venues & clash**: spread across a car-scale city — Dubai Opera, Coca-Cola
  Arena, Mall of the Emirates theatre, clubs; 2–3 shows per evening across
  distant venues. Lineup-picking with traffic, not a schedule grid.
- **Ticketing & data**: per-show, multi-vendor — mostly
  [Platinumlist](https://dubaicomedyfestival.platinumlist.net/) (which runs an
  aggregating microsite), plus venue box offices and Ticketmaster.ae for some
  shows. The [shows page](https://www.dubaicomedyfest.ae/shows) is
  server-rendered Squarespace carrying every show's date, venue, language,
  price and vendor link in plain HTML — the easiest large-festival page to
  read mechanically in the whole census.

## The structural exhibits

Festivals that mark out the edges of the taxonomy — none is a planner market,
and each pins down one shape the census keeps producing.

### Great Outdoors Comedy Festival — the music-festival pole, confirmed

The hypothesis the census raised, confirmed and then some: GOCF is not even a
serial tour but a **franchise running parallel one-stage city productions on
shared weekends** — [seven 2026 stops](https://greatoutdoorscomedyfestival.com/):
Edmonton *and* Winnipeg both 17–19 July, Calgary *and* Vancouver 28–30 August
with Spokane the same weekend, Halifax 6–9 August, Mississauga 11–13
September; 2027 dates already on sale. Owned and run by
[Trixstar](https://greatoutdoorscomedyfestival.com/about), an Edmonton
promoter; since 2021 it claims 400,000+ cumulative attendees. One outdoor
stage per city (Vancouver's Stanley Park permit caps at
[10,000/day](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/the-great-outdoors-comedy-festival-proposal-stanley-park)),
two shows a day (matinee + evening), each a one-off bill of touring headliners
(Bill Burr, Matt Rife, Pete Davidson tiers), grounds cleared between shows,
explicitly [no application process](https://greatoutdoorscomedyfestival.com/gocf-faqs)
for performers, GA/VIP tiers, no re-entry, 18+/19+. Ticketing is
[Tixr-only](https://greatoutdoorscomedyfestival.com/cities/vancouver); the
Webflow site is fully server-rendered. **Scheduling problem: none by design —
the only decision is which city you are in.** This is what "comedy festival"
means when the shape is literally a music festival's.

### The TV-taping festivals — Winnipeg and Halifax

Canada's two legacy festivals are shaped end to end by broadcast production,
and they show what a "festival" is when its real product is television:

- **[Winnipeg Comedy Festival](https://www.winnipegcomedyfestival.com/about-us)**
  (annual since 2002, produced by the nonprofit Gas Station Arts Centre):
  ["30+ shows. 9 venues. 85 comics"](https://www.winnipegcomedyfestival.com/news/post/105)
  over 7 days, anchored by five "Mega Shows" **recorded for CBC** at the
  Burton Cummings Theatre — celebrity host + six comics, PG while cameras
  roll, in a venue chosen for camera/crew needs (which forces Ticketmaster;
  everything else sells through local ticketer 3Common, per
  [its FAQ](https://www.winnipegcomedyfestival.com/faqs)). The broadcast
  audience ("over 2 million viewers annually — CBC Television's highest-rated
  comedy festival series") dwarfs the live one. 2–3 parallel rooms at peak;
  lineup-picking.
- **[Halifax ComedyFest](https://www.halifaxcomedyfest.ca/about-the-fest.html)**
  (annual since 1995): self-described as "one of only three major comedy
  festivals broadcast nationally in prime time on CBC Television… as a
  six-episode series"; [its application page](https://www.halifaxcomedyfest.ca/apply.html)
  demands "corporate clean" audition tapes and caps international bookings

752	  outright in 2024 by its owner's insolvency, then relaunched under new
753	  ownership — same city, same district, new company. Quebec City's festival
754	  kept running while its *name* changed (ComediHa! Fest → Juste pour rire
755	  Québec).
756	- **Operator dies, festival forks**: Leicester 2026 delivered, then the
757	  charity behind it liquidated; February 2027 has **two** claimants to the
758	  same slot and venues. "Which festival is Leicester" is currently
759	  unanswerable.
760	- **Experiments and departures**: JFL Paris appears dropped (404s, no 2026
761	  edition found) despite sitting on the tracker; JFL Singapore's second
762	  edition is unconfirmed; SF Sketchfest skipped 2021–22 (COVID).
763	- **Rovers**: Skankfest has moved Queens → Houston → Las Vegas → New
764	  Orleans (the brand, not the city, is the fixture); Great Outdoors is a
765	  franchise whose "city" is a list; the SF and Seattle competitions tour
766	  their own regions by design.
767	
768	The modelling implication: **key a festival calendar on city + month slot,
769	but track the operator separately from the brand** — the three failure modes
770	above (skipped year, renamed brand, contested succession) are all invisible
771	to a calendar that stores only "festival X happens each February".
772	
773	## Concurrent-festival clusters
774	
775	Which comedy festivals sit inside a bigger city moment — the owner's "the
776	city is a bigger draw" question. Three patterns emerged:
777	
778	**Real clusters (the Edinburgh property).** Cities where other festivals
779	overlap the comedy window and change the visitor's calculus:
780	
781	| Comedy festival | Overlapping in the same city |
782	|---|---|
783	| Edinburgh Fringe (Aug) | seven other festivals — owned by [edinburgh-festival-season/](../edinburgh-festival-season/README.md) |
784	| Adelaide Fringe (Feb–Mar) | Adelaide Festival, WOMADelaide, Writers' Week — "Mad March", on [festmaxxing-environments/](../festmaxxing-environments/README.md) |
785	| Brighton Fringe (May) | Brighton Festival (105 curated events, 1–25 May) and The Great Escape (30+ music venues, 13–16 May), both wholly inside the Fringe's month |
786	| NZICF, Auckland leg (May) | NZ Music Month all month + Auckland Writers Festival inside the window — [The Spinoff](https://thespinoff.co.nz/pop-culture/06-05-2026/auckland-has-a-problem-everything-awesome-is-happening-in-may-all-at-once): "everything awesome is happening in May, all at once" |
787	| JFL Montreal (Jul) | Fantasia film festival in near-total overlap, Nuits d'Afrique on the first weekend, Complètement Cirque ending just before, Jazz Fest just before that — the Quartier des Spectacles is a festival machine all July |
788	| SXSW comedy (Mar) | the cluster *is* the festival: film + music + interactive + comedy on one badge, one downtown |
789	
790	**Amplifiers, not clusters.** Melbourne's MICF window brushes the Food &
791	Wine Festival, the Flower & Garden Show and the AFL season — more reasons
792	to be in town, but nothing a cross-festival planner would join. Sydney's
793	window touches the Easter Show and Writers' Festival with Vivid just after.
794	
795	**The festival is the draw.** Leicester in February, LA in Netflix week,
796	SF Sketchfest in January, Dubai in October (GITEX moved to December) — the
797	comedy festival stands alone. Two curiosities: Toronto's JFL deliberately
798	sits *after* TIFF and gets the autumn to itself, with the micro-festival
799	WHAT THE FESTIVAL! nesting inside JFL's own dates; and the US November
800	pile-up (NYCF, 312, Boston, Skankfest in one fortnight) is concurrency
801	across *cities* — the same touring headliners circulating — not within one.

803	## Ticketing and data across the circuit
804	
805	The owner asked for ticketing, scraping and organizers per festival — the
806	dossiers carry each; this section is the cross-festival picture.
807	
808	**Ticketing splits into central-basket festivals and fan-out festivals.**
809	Central, festival-owned box offices: Edinburgh (Tikketr), Adelaide (its own
810	FringeTIX/AVR), MICF (its own Umbraco store), JFL's hahaha.com family (its
811	own "Nova" platform + Stripe, one basket per city), Brighton and Leicester
812	(Eventotron + Stripe), Galway (self-built), plus pass-gated singletons
813	(SXSW badge, Skankfest's Tixr pass, Moontower's badge on the venue's
814	Tessitura). Fan-out festivals hand the buyer to a different seller per
815	show: Sydney and NZICF (up to four agents), NYCF (Ticketmaster/ATG/house),
816	Netflix Is A Joke (**12+ vendors** counted from its own payload),
817	Nashville/312 (Etix/AXS/TM), Dubai (Platinumlist + venues), JFL Sydney (six
818	sellers). The vendor names recur — Tixr (Great Outdoors, Halifax,
819	Skankfest), Eventbrite, Showpass, Fienta, See Tickets, TicketSource,
820	SISTIC, Spektrix (Aberdeen — the same vendor whose public API the
821	[edinburgh-fringe-ticketing/](../edinburgh-fringe-ticketing/README.md) census found at
822	Edinburgh's Traverse), and post-collapse Leicester's challenger runs on
823	TixEvery, which pays performers directly. Red61, which powers Edinburgh's
824	venue side, appears nowhere else in this census.
825	
826	Two product observations sit in that split:
827	
828	- **A planner is worth more where ticketing fans out** — at MICF or Adelaide
829	  one basket already holds the whole trip; at NZICF, Sydney or Netflix Is A
830	  Joke *nothing* unifies the trip except a planner.
831	- **But data is hardest exactly where ticketing fans out** — the fan-out
832	  festivals have no single machine surface, so per-festival adapters are
833	  unavoidable there.
834	
835	**Data reachability, ranked from the fetches** (every entry verified
836	first-hand this pass):
837	
838	1. **MICF** — unauthenticated JSON APIs (show search, venues with
839	   capacities) plus per-performance status flags embedded in show pages:
840	   near enough the Edinburgh scraper's field set, no scraping gymnastics.
841	2. **Leicester + Brighton** — the **same Eventotron WordPress substrate**
842	   exposing identical open REST APIs (`/wp-json/wp/v2/events` with
843	   dates/genres/venues taxonomies): one adapter, two festivals — and the
844	   registration layer under many more fringes worldwide is Eventotron too.
845	3. **Netflix Is A Joke** — the whole dataset (times, venues, lat/long,
846	   capacities, ticket URLs) inlined in one server-rendered page: a single
847	   fetch.
848	4. **NYCF** — live open WordPress REST API.
849	5. **Clean server-rendered HTML**: Dubai (every show's date/venue/language/
850	   price/vendor in plain HTML), Great Outdoors, Winnipeg, Nashville, 312,
851	   Sydney + Perth (one shared Century WordPress codebase — one adapter for
852	   both), NZICF (SilverStripe).
853	6. **Hard or fragile**: JFL (client-side HTML fragments, no structured API,
854	   and **listings are ephemeral — city sites were emptied within weeks of
855	   the festival ending**, so capture must happen in-season); Adelaide
856	   (in-season server HTML only, no API found); SF Sketchfest
857	   (captcha-walled site; the Eventbrite organizer account is the practical
858	   surface); SXSW (client-rendered SPA); Galway (a Base44 app-builder SPA);
859	   Tokyo (client-rendered lineup; Fienta pages are the surface).
860	
861	**What nobody exposes**: per-performance availability. MICF's embedded
862	session flags (sold-out/preview/cheap-night) are the one census-wide
863	sighting of Edinburgh-scraper-grade availability data; everywhere else the
864	best case is a binary sold-out badge on a sales page. The two-source shape
865	[festmaxxing-environments/](../festmaxxing-environments/README.md)
866	worried about (a listings source plus a separate availability source) is
867	not the general case — the general case is *worse*: one source for
868	listings, and no availability source at all.

870	## The film adjacency — surveyed light, on the owner's direction
871	
872	Film festivals run on the same two axes as comedy, and the owner asked for
873	the planner-complex ones flagged without deep research (2026-09-01; each
874	entry is one look, not a dossier). The bar: multi-venue, many parallel
875	screenings, public single tickets, ~8+ days, ideally **repeat screenings**
876	— the recurrence property that turns triage into optimization.
877	
878	The strongest planner-fits, ranked:
879	
880	1. **Berlinale** (Berlin, 11 days each Feb) — film's closest thing to a
881	   fringe: 274 films in 2026, **each screening up to five times**
882	   ([its own entry guidelines](https://www.berlinale.de/en/film-entry/guidelines/general-guidelines.html)),
883	   fully public tickets at €9–15 released online three days before each
884	   screening, venues spread across the city — and an official
885	   [**"My Festival Planner"**](https://www.berlinale.de/en/programme/festival-planner.html)
886	   (favourites → schedule → iCal), the most planner-shaped official tool
887	   seen in any circuit this wiki covers.
888	2. **TIFF** (Toronto, 11 days each Sep) — 200+ films, ~2 public screenings
889	   each, clustered downtown venues, an official app with favourites and
890	   in-app tickets — and the only healthy **third-party festival planner
891	   found in film**: [tiffr.com](https://2026.tiffr.com/), TIFF-only, one
892	   site per year, alive for 2026.
893	3. **MIFF** (Melbourne, **18 days** each Aug) — 275+ films, ~10 venues,
894	   180,000+ attendees ([ACMI](https://www.acmi.net.au/whats-on/miff-2026/))
895	   — the longest major, in a city we already track for MICF (different
896	   months; no overlap).
897	4. **IFFR Rotterdam** (11 days, ~480 films, 300k+ admissions citywide),
898	   **SIFF Seattle** (11 days, 203 films, a walkable multi-screen cluster,
899	   the most-attended US festival), **BFI London** (12 days, ~240 features,
900	   7 venues), **Locarno** (11 days, public, an 8,000-seat open-air piazza),
901	   **Sundance** (11 days, $35 public single tickets, two towns — **moving
902	   to Boulder for 2027** on a ten-year deal, per
903	   [THR](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/sundance-boulder-colorado-move-from-park-city-1236135102/) —
904	   the census's rare city *move*), **Sydney FF** (12 days, 13 spread
905	   venues, on Eventival), **Busan** (10 days, 329 films on 31 screens in
906	   one cluster, sell-out-in-minutes scarcity).
907	5. Second tier: Fantasia (Montreal, 18 days, clustered, selective repeats),
908	   IDFA, Hot Docs, Glasgow.
909	
910	**The Israeli circuit** (owner question, 2026-09-01: does Docaviv fit the
911	mold?). It does — Berlinale-shaped at half the scale — and it is not even
912	Israel's strongest fit:
913	
914	- **Jerusalem Film Festival** (11 days each July, 43rd edition
915	  [9–19 Jul 2026](https://jff.org.il/en/article/91360)) — the best planner
916	  fit in the country: 200+ films from 60 countries, 22–28 screenings a day
917	  across five halls (the Cinematheque's four plus Lev Smadar), films
918	  verified screening twice across the window (e.g. the
919	  [17 July](https://jff.org.il/en/festival-calendar/2026-07-17) and
920	  [18 July](https://jff.org.il/en/festival-calendar/2026-07-18) calendar
921	  days share four titles), singles at ₪48 (member ₪43) with 6- and
922	  10-ticket [passes](https://jff.org.il/he/%D7%9E%D7%90%D7%9E%D7%A8/85822),
923	  ~70,000 expected attendees, running since 1984 — and a real urgency
924	  engine: the
925	  [Jerusalem Post reports](https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/culture/article-900392)
926	  more than three-quarters of its international films have no Israeli
927	  distributor, so the festival screening is likely the only one.
928	- **Docaviv** (Tel Aviv, 10 days late May–June, since 1998) — 123 film
929	  pages on the 2026 site including shorts (press blurbs say "over 80
930	  films"), each film screened 2–3 times across the window (premiere plus
931	  [1–2 additional screenings](https://nfct.org.il/blog/docaviv-2026/)),
932	  centred on the five-hall Tel Aviv Cinematheque with ten satellite venues
933	  [listed for 2026](https://www.docaviv.co.il/%D7%9E%D7%A4%D7%94-%D7%95%D7%9E%D7%99%D7%93%D7%A2-%D7%A9%D7%99%D7%9E%D7%95%D7%A9%D7%99/),
934	  singles at [₪49 (~€12.50) with carnets down to ~₪31](https://www.docaviv.co.il/tickets-and-benefits/),
935	  ~40,000 attendance — Oscar-qualifying, self-described Israel's largest
936	  international film festival.
937	- **Haifa International Film Festival** (8 days, 42nd edition
938	  [26 Sep – 3 Oct 2026](https://www.haifaff.co.il/eng), since 1983) — ~170
939	  films, 4–5 parallel halls
940	  [clustered on one Carmel Center boulevard](https://www.haifaff.co.il/eng/Screening_Halls)
941	  (five of seven within ~400 m), films screened ~2×, singles ₪49 — and it
942	  runs **inside the Sukkot national holiday week**
943	  ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haifa_International_Film_Festival)),
944	  a built-in "planning my time off" audience.
945	
946	The rest of the Israeli calendar (TLVFest, Solidarity, Epos, Utopia, Animix,
947	Cinema South Sderot, the student festival) is one-cinematheque scale. The
948	shared limit across all three majors: everything concentrates in a
949	cinematheque hub, so travel never binds, and daily volume tops out near 28
950	screenings against the Fringe's hundreds — a planner is useful there, not
951	indispensable.
952	
953	Failing the bar, for the record: **Cannes** (no meaningful public
954	ticketing), **Venice** (public tickets exist but premiere-driven, industry
955	absorbs the seats), **SXSW Film** (badge-first, cut to 7 days), **Fantastic
956	Fest** (one venue, badge-driven).
957	
958	What the light pass established for the taxonomy: **repeat screenings are
959	the norm at the big public film festivals and absent at the premiere
960	festivals** — the same recurrence split as comedy's fringe-vs-showcase; the
961	**Fantasia × JFL overlap gives Montreal eleven shared days** of film ×
962	comedy co-planning (the one such city found); and film's third-party
963	planner category is one TIFF-only specimen — as empty as comedy's outside
964	Edinburgh. A future film expansion would start at Berlinale/TIFF/MIFF, and
965	each needs the deep pass this survey deliberately skipped.
